documents.title: Proposed AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Draft university-wide guidelines for the whole community on confidentiality, bias, disclosure, accountability, equity, IP, safety and AI notetaking. For classrooms it sets no ban or mandate and lets faculty prohibit, allow with attribution or encourage AI.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say the "University does not restrict the use of AI tools in the classroom" and that "Faculty and instructors may choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage generative AI use," so the decision rests with instructors and the document itself is delegates.

units.why: The Purpose section says the university must "equip students and graduates" with tools for a world of emerging technologies; this is a career-preparation rationale for AI, so P44 and informs.
units.anchor: Villanova has an obligation to equip students and graduates

units.why: "foster an ethical and responsible approach to AI" states the purpose and principles of an institution-wide framework, so P56.
units.anchor: foster an ethical and responsible approach to AI

units.why: The scope sentence says the guidelines apply to "all members of the Villanova University community"; it sets coverage of the framework, so P56 rather than P61 (it defines people, not AI).
units.anchor: apply to the use of AI tools by all members of the Villanova University community

units.why: "This document is not a final policy but will be updated" says the guidance is provisional and will be revised, P54.
units.anchor: not a final policy but will be updated as AI technology

units.why: "intended to complement existing policies on ethics, privacy, security, and compliance" ties the guidelines to existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: complement existing policies on ethics, privacy, security, and compliance

units.why: The definitions of "AI System" and "Generative AI" set what the guidelines cover, so P61 and informs; the mention of "Github Copilot" embedded in other software is extra.
units.anchor: offerings that are embedded in other software, such as Github Copilot
units.fit_note: Also says generative AI embedded in other software such as Github Copilot is covered, touching P07.

units.why: "AI tools should be used within the Acceptable Use and Data Classifications policies" ties AI use to existing university policies; P77 over P50 because it is about compliance.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used within the

units.why: "You should not enter data that is classified as Restricted or Private" is a data-protection prohibition (FERPA, HIPAA), so P50.
units.anchor: You should not enter data that is classified as Restricted or Private
units.frag_end: patient data under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
units.policy: Users should not enter data classified as Restricted or Private, including non-public student data and information subject to federal or state laws, into AI tools.

units.why: "Any information provided to third-party, public generative AI tools is considered public" explains the data risk of public tools, P50 and informs.
units.anchor: Any information provided to third-party, public generative AI tools is considered public
units.frag_end: personal ChatGPT account is considered a public AI tool

units.why: Sensitive data may go into AI only after the "Office of Information Security" approves the tool and legal reviews a contract; this is vetting of tools by named offices, so P65 rather than P50.
units.anchor: without the tool having been assessed and approved by the Office of Information Security
units.frag_end: reviewed by the Office of General Counsel
units.policy: Sensitive data should not be entered into generative AI tools unless the tool has been assessed and approved by the Office of Information Security and a contract reviewed by the Office of General Counsel is in place.

units.why: The bias passage notes tools are trained on unmoderated text and "can result in the production of biased and other unintended content," a bias harm, so P53.
units.anchor: This can result in the production of biased and other unintended content.

units.why: The sentence says integrity detection tools have "biases by incorrectly flagging writing by students for whom English is not their first-learned language"; it warns that detectors are unreliable, so P39 with the bias angle noted.
units.anchor: certain academic integrity detection tools are known to have biases
units.fit_note: Frames detector unreliability as bias against non-native English writers rather than as a rule not to rely on detectors.

units.why: "Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool" is a disclosure rule for everyone, P24.
units.anchor: Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool
units.frag_end: how AI was used to create the work product
units.policy: Be transparent about AI use: disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool and, if appropriate, how AI was used.

units.why: "Non-disclosure could be considered misrepresentation or plagiarism" makes failure to disclose the violation, so P28.
units.anchor: Non-disclosure could be considered misrepresentation or plagiarism

units.why: "All students, faculty, and staff are responsible for any content published... that includes any AI-generated material" makes users own what they publish, P29.
units.anchor: responsible for any content published, shared, or otherwise developed that includes any AI-generated material

units.why: "AI-generated content... can be inaccurate, false, biased, misleading, fabricated (hallucinations)... Always verify the information" tells users to verify AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Always verify the information and exercise caution.
units.frag_end: Always verify the information and exercise caution.

units.why: "AI-generated content may contain copyrighted material" warns of IP risk in AI output, so P52.
units.anchor: AI-generated content may contain copyrighted material

units.why: The data-scraping note says public data "will likely be scraped" and legality is unresolved; it is an ethical and legal concern about AI, closest to P53.
units.anchor: any data posted publicly will likely be scraped
units.frag_end: used in this way by third parties
units.fit_note: Concerns scraping of public data for model training and unresolved legality, not bias or environmental cost.

units.why: "AI tools should be used in ways that do not create or reinforce systemic disadvantages" is an equity commitment, P51 (access and fairness); P97 is only about disabilities.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used in ways that do not create or reinforce systemic disadvantages
units.frag_end: socioeconomic status, or other protected characteristics

units.why: "consider the needs of users with disabilities and ensure compliance with accessibility standards" is accessibility of AI use, P97.
units.anchor: consider the needs of users with disabilities and ensure compliance with accessibility standards

units.why: "Faculty and staff should strive to provide alternative methods of engagement" for people with limited AI access is an equity provision, P51.
units.anchor: provide alternative methods of engagement for students and employees who may have limited access

units.why: "assume that AI-generated text, images, and code may not be eligible for copyright protection or may inadvertently infringe" is a copyright and ownership caution, P52.
units.anchor: may not be eligible for copyright protection or may inadvertently infringe on existing copyrights
units.frag_start: Faculty, students, and staff should assume

units.why: "Any AI-assisted content should be properly attributed" is an attribution rule, P24.
units.anchor: Any AI-assisted content should be properly attributed

units.why: Users should consult the IP and Copyright policies before using AI-generated material, which sends them to existing university policy, P77.
units.anchor: consult the University’s Intellectual Property Policy and Copyright Infringement and Illegal File Sharing Policy
units.policy: Users consult the University’s Intellectual Property Policy and Copyright Infringement and Illegal File Sharing Policy before incorporating AI-generated materials into their work.

units.why: "some publishers and funding agencies may have specific guidelines regarding AI-generated content" tells researchers to defer to venue and funder rules, P62.
units.anchor: some publishers and funding agencies may have specific guidelines regarding AI-generated content
units.frag_start: faculty and researchers should be aware

units.why: "they should not replace critical thinking and foundational learning" says AI must not replace thinking, P32.
units.anchor: they should not replace critical thinking and foundational learning

units.why: "Overreliance on AI tools for tasks such as writing, coding, or research analysis may impede skill development" explains that AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill, P41.
units.anchor: Overreliance on AI tools for tasks such as writing, coding, or research analysis

units.why: "verifying the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated information before use" tells users to verify output, P31.
units.anchor: verifying the accuracy and reliability of AI-generated information before use

units.why: "AI is used as a tool rather than a substitute for human cognition and problem-solving" keeps humans as the primary thinkers, P32.
units.anchor: AI is used as a tool rather than a substitute for human cognition

units.why: Users "should report any suspected misuse to the Office of Information Security" sets a reporting channel for AI misuse, P71.
units.anchor: report any suspected misuse to the Office of Information Security

units.anchor: can be used maliciously to deceive, manipulate, or harm individuals

units.anchor: should undergo ethical review and risk assessment
units.frag_start: Any AI applications used in research

units.why: "AI-driven automation in decision-making should be carefully evaluated" so it does not pose risks to people; the nearest type is P73 though the passage does not say a human must decide.
units.anchor: AI-driven automation in decision-making should be carefully evaluated
units.fit_note: Calls for evaluation of automated decisions but does not state that a human must review and decide.

units.why: "should not create or distribute deepfake content without explicit consent" bans deceptive or harmful AI media, P74.
units.anchor: should not create or distribute deepfake content without explicit consent
units.policy: Community members should not create or distribute deepfake content without explicit consent from the individuals depicted.

units.why: AI media used for "research, education, or creative projects should be clearly labeled as synthetic content," a labeling duty; closest is P24 disclosure.
units.anchor: should be clearly labeled as synthetic content
units.policy: Any AI-generated media used for research, education, or creative projects should be clearly labeled as synthetic content.
units.fit_note: Labeling of synthetic media to prevent misinformation, rather than acknowledging AI help in a submission.

units.why: Notetaking tools that record speech require "notice, such as including it in a syllabus or announcing its use before recording," which is notice before AI recording, P86.
units.anchor: they must provide notice, such as including it in a syllabus

units.why: "If an individual objects to being recorded, an alternative note-taking method should be explored" is part of the recording-consent rule, P86.
units.anchor: an alternative note-taking method should be explored and considered
units.frag_start: If an individual objects to being

units.anchor: review AI-generated notes before widespread distribution

units.anchor: may choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage generative AI use

units.why: "does not restrict the use of AI tools in the classroom" is the university-level default of no ban, a permissive default, P02; the choice among options is coded separately as P04.
units.anchor: Villanova University does not restrict the use of AI tools in the classroom.

units.why: "AI should be used consistent with The Code of Academic Integrity and Code of Student Conduct" ties classroom AI to existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: AI should be used consistent with The

units.frag_start: Faculty and instructors should be clear
units.fit_note: Asks for clear communication of AI policy, not specifically a syllabus statement.

units.why: "Students are expected to seek clarification from faculty as needed" is ask-when-unsure, P10.
units.anchor: Students are expected to seek clarification from faculty as needed.

units.why: "Individual colleges, departments, or instructors may have specific guidance" lets units set their own rules, P85.

documents.title: The Code of Academic Integrity
documents.summary: The university integrity code defines AI-assisted work as dishonesty when unsanctioned or undocumented, and bars AI doing central requirements without instructor permission and full citation. Course-level rules are left to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The Code treats "work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance" as dishonesty and bars AI on central requirements "without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation," so AI is banned unless permitted; faculty can set course rules but the document itself sets this default, hence restrict.

units.why: Academic dishonesty includes representing "work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance" as one's own, so such AI work is classed as dishonesty, P36.
units.anchor: work generated through unsanctioned and/or undocumented artificial intelligence (A.I.) assistance

units.why: "students must submit work that they have completed themselves in accordance with the guidelines for the course" says submitted work must be the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: students must submit work that they have completed themselves
units.frag_start: To uphold academic integrity, students must

units.why: "faculty may set specific rules about what is and is not allowed in a particular course" gives AI rules to faculty, P04.
units.anchor: faculty may set specific rules about what is and is not allowed

units.why: "Students must follow faculty-issued instructions for courses and assignments and may be penalized" binds students to each course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: Students must follow faculty-issued instructions for courses and assignments
units.frag_end: Code of Academic Integrity if they do not

units.why: "When in doubt, students should ask for clarification from their instructor before turning in the assignment" is ask-when-unsure, P10.
units.anchor: students should ask for clarification from their instructor before turning in the assignment
units.frag_start: When in doubt, students should ask

units.why: The purpose says "By consulting with their instructors, students can resolve any questions," advice to ask instructors early, P10.
units.anchor: By consulting with their instructors, students can resolve any questions
units.fit_note: General integrity advice, not specifically about AI.

units.why: Students "shall rely on their own mastery" and not get help "not explicitly approved by the instructor"; outside help is barred unless approved, the fallback P06, though AI is not named here.
units.anchor: not attempt to receive help in any way not explicitly approved by the instructor
units.frag_start: students shall rely on their own mastery
units.fit_note: Covers outside help generally, not AI by name.

units.why: Using "A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment" without "explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation" is cheating, a ban on AI doing the work, P19.
units.anchor: using the assistance of A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment
units.frag_start: This includes using the assistance of
units.policy: Using A.I. text generators to perform central requirements of an assignment (reading, synthesizing, interpreting, writing, coding, programming) without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components is cheating.
units.fit_note: Also lists reading and synthesizing as central requirements and requires both permission and citation.

units.why: The same sentence requires "explicit permission of the instructor" for AI use, making AI banned unless an instructor allows it, the fallback rule P06.
units.anchor: without both the explicit permission of the instructor and complete attribution and citation

units.why: "complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components" makes citing AI a condition of any permitted use, P24.
units.anchor: complete attribution and citation of A.I.-assisted components

units.why: "Please consult with your instructor if you are uncertain whether outside sources/support, including A.I. support, are allowed" is ask-when-unsure, P10.
units.anchor: Please consult with your instructor if you are uncertain whether outside sources/support
units.frag_end: allowed in a course or on an assignment

units.why: Fabrication bans using "falsify, invent, or use in a misleading way any information, data, or citations"; a general deception rule, P74, with no AI named.
units.anchor: Students shall not falsify, invent, or use in a misleading way any information
units.fit_note: Does not name AI; a general fabrication ban.

units.why: Plagiarism "includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I." so AI output is treated as plagiarism if unacknowledged, P36.
units.anchor: This includes work generated by or originating from non-human sources, such as A.I.

units.why: "using either the work of another person or of A.I. without reference or acknowledgement" requires acknowledging AI like any other source, P45.
units.anchor: using either the work of another person or of A.I. without reference or acknowledgement

units.why: "borrowing sentences, phrases, and paragraphs from outside sources, including A.I. text generators" is named as unacknowledged appropriation, a ban on copying AI output into one's work, P19.
units.anchor: borrowing sentences, phrases, and paragraphs from outside sources, including A.I. text generators
units.frag_start: Unacknowledged appropriation also includes borrowing sentences

units.why: Sources that "require citation or acknowledgment" include "ideas, summaries, drafts, data, code, and text generated via A.I.", specifying what AI output must be cited, P24.
units.anchor: ideas, summaries, drafts, data, code, and text generated via A.I.

units.why: Students "should contact the instructor to discuss this prior to submission" if uncertain whether they acknowledged sources adequately, ask-when-unsure, P10.
units.anchor: they should contact the instructor to discuss this prior to submission
units.fit_note: Concerns source acknowledgement in general; AI is named elsewhere in the section.

units.why: "it is the student’s responsibility to authenticate authorship" puts the burden of proving authorship on the student, P29.
units.anchor: it is the student’s responsibility to authenticate authorship
units.frag_start: If questions arise about the authorship
units.fit_note: Also sets who bears the burden of proving authorship in a dispute.

units.anchor: students must follow their instructor’s directions regarding any collaboration with other students
units.frag_start: students must follow their instructor’s directions
units.frag_end: collaboration with other students to complete the work
units.fit_note: About collaboration with other students, not AI.

units.anchor: take their case to the Board of Academic Integrity
units.frag_start: Students who receive an academic integrity violation
units.fit_note: General appeal right for any integrity violation, not AI-specific.

units.frag_start: The instructor may impose a grade penalty

units.anchor: Students who violate the Code of Academic Integrity are also referred to their dean
units.frag_end: to their dean for a University penalty
units.fit_note: Describes referral to the dean; the passage does not use the word report.

units.why: The revision history ("Approved by Provost and Council of Deans: August 16, 2023") says how and when the Code, with its AI language, was adopted, P84.
units.anchor: Revisions approved by Provost and Council Deans: April 26, 2023

documents.unit: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
documents.title: ECE syllabus outline template: AI Policy block
tiers: Permitted for listed uses (first draft, outline, other)
documents.summary: Template for ECE syllabi giving instructors three alternative AI statements (ban, allow, allow for listed uses) and a disclosure paragraph for any allowed use. It is generic, not one course policy.
documents.stance_why: The block tells instructors to choose "one of the following statements" - "not permitted," "allowed," or "permitted as follows" - so it offers templates and sets no stance of its own, which makes it delegates with tiers.

units.why: The template tells an instructor to choose among statements; letting each instructor pick the AI rule is P04.
units.anchor: choosing one of the following statements, modifying as desired
units.frag_start: you should edit this part, choosing

units.why: The first option bans AI-generated content in the course, P01.
units.anchor: The use of AI-generated content is not permitted in this course.

units.why: "Its use will result in an academic integrity violation and a zero on the assignment" states a concrete penalty, P37.
units.anchor: Its use will result in an academic integrity violation and a zero on the assignment.

units.why: The second option, "AI-generated content is allowed in this course", is a permissive default, P02.
units.anchor: The use of AI-generated content is allowed in this course.

units.why: The third option permits AI only "(a) for generating a first draft or (b) for generating an outline or (c) for generating XXX", a closed list of tasks, P107.
units.anchor: permitted as follows: (a) for generating a first draft or (b) for generating an outline

units.why: "you must identify the AI tool used to assist in generating your work" even after editing, a disclosure duty, P24.
units.anchor: you must identify the AI tool used to assist in generating your work
units.frag_start: Even if you have significantly edited

units.anchor: name of the tool, date used, and prompts used to generate the output

units.anchor: you must keep a copy of the original output and provide it when requested

units.why: "you are responsible for authenticating your authorship" puts proof of authorship on the student, P29.
units.anchor: you are responsible for authenticating your authorship
units.frag_start: If questions arise about the authorship

units.why: "You should save evidence of your authorial process, such as drafts, notes, version histories, and complete transcripts of AI assistance" is a log-keeping duty, P26.
units.anchor: save evidence of your authorial process, such as drafts, notes, version histories

units.why: The template points to "Guidelines for Students Regarding Responsible Academic Use of AI-Generated Material," a pointer to more guidance, P115.
units.anchor: Guidelines for Students Regarding Responsible Academic Use of AI-Generated Material

notes: Coder B. The Guidelines are headed "Proposed" and say they are not a final policy. The ECE block is a template with LaTeX markup, not a course policy. Code stance is a judgment call: restrict because it bans unsanctioned AI on central requirements by default, while leaving course rules to faculty.
